title: Active Order
description_html:
You are managing a hierarchy of entities. There is one root entity. Each entity may have children, and children are ordered by the time they were added: earlier children come before later children.

Entities can become inactive, but inactive entities should remain in the hierarchy because their children may still be active.

Implement a data structure that supports:

  • addChild(parentId, childId)
  • markInactive(entityId)
  • getActiveOrder()

getActiveOrder() should return all active entities in hierarchy order:

  • Start from the root.
  • Visit an entity before its children.
  • Visit children from oldest to newest.
  • Skip inactive entities themselves, but still traverse their children.

Example

root = "A"

addChild("A", "B")
addChild("A", "C")
addChild("B", "D")

Hierarchy:
A
├── B
│   └── D
└── C

getActiveOrder() -> ["A", "B", "D", "C"]

markInactive("B")

getActiveOrder() -> ["A", "D", "C"]

Approach hint

Keep a Map<id, Node> where each Node stores { active: boolean, children: id[] }. addChild pushes to parent.children (preserving insertion order). markInactive flips the flag. getActiveOrder is pre-order DFS that emits the current node only when active, but always recurses into its children. Patterns: LC 588 (Design FS), LC 589 (N-ary pre-order), LC 1110 (delete + preserve children).
